tour.title: Project Overview via PLAN
tour.description: Start with the coordinator PLAN.md, the closest thing this codebase has to a project-level overview in the graph. It defines what ree-v3 is (the active V3 implementation substrate for the REE research programme), lays out the target architecture as a stdlib coordinator + a fleet of runners, and specifies the HTTP contract, SQLite schema, and phased rollout that the rest of the coordinator half implements. Reading this first anchors the two halves you will meet: cognitive substrate under ree_core/ and fleet orchestration under coordinator/.

tour.title: REEAgent Orchestrator
tour.description: REEAgent is the master cognitive orchestrator. This ~9500-line class assembles every substrate you will meet in the next steps (latent stack, E1/E2/E3 predictors, hippocampal module, residue field, cingulate cluster, PFC analogs, sleep) and drives them through one canonical loop: SENSE -> E1 tick -> E2 tick -> E3 tick -> SELECT -> ACT -> RESIDUE -> REPLAY -> OFFLINE. Every subsequent step is a subsystem this file wires together, so keep the loop shape in mind — it is the backbone of the whole tour.
tour.languageLesson: Python: this is a striking example of a monolithic orchestrator class over a large graph of pluggable submodules. Each subsystem is instantiated conditionally behind a config flag, letting experiments turn mechanisms on and off without editing the loop — a pattern that lets a research substrate stay experimentally reversible while growing to thousands of lines.

tour.title: Central Configuration Surface
tour.description: The whole architecture is parameterised through one central config surface. REEConfig aggregates per-substrate dataclasses (LatentStackConfig, E1Config, E2Config, E3Config, HippocampalConfig, ResidueConfig, HeartbeatConfig, environment config) and exposes a from_dims factory that resolves cross-cutting master switches. It has the highest fan-in in the code graph (imported by ~10 other modules), so understanding its shape unlocks how every mechanism above and below is toggled. Experiment scripts build a REEConfig, hand it to REEAgent, and the whole cognitive stack is configured in one place.
tour.languageLesson: Python dataclasses: nested dataclass configs are used here as a typed, introspectable knob-set — a scalable alternative to argparse. The from_dims factory pattern lets one call resolve derived defaults (e.g. E3Config.commit_threshold defaulting from world_dim), turning a large flag-set into a small factory-call surface.

tour.title: The Latent Stack (Perception)
tour.description: The latent stack is REE's perception layer, sitting at the edge between environment observations and everything downstream. It implements the SD-005 z_self vs z_world split (encoders for body-state vs world-state), the SD-010/SD-011 harm-stream encoders (sensory z_harm and affective z_harm_a), the SD-007 reafference predictor for self-caused perceptual change, and the shared z_beta/z_theta/z_delta context bindings E1 will read. Every predictor and every downstream mechanism reads latents produced here, so a bug in stack.py silently corrupts everything.
tour.languageLesson: PyTorch: this file shows a common pattern in research code — many small nn.Module encoders composed into one 'stack' module rather than one large network. It lets an experiment freeze one channel (e.g. z_self), swap another (e.g. an SD-070 z_world variant), and measure the isolated effect without retraining the whole model.

tour.title: E1 Deep + E2 Fast Predictors
tour.description: Building on the latents from Step 4, this step covers the two forward models: E1 is a slow, deep long-horizon predictor built on an LSTM over the latent stack with a cue-indexed ContextMemory (SD-016) for schema readout; E2 is a fast per-step predictor for self and world transitions with contrastive world-forward losses and counterfactual rollouts. E1 answers 'what schema is this?' at a coherence timescale; E2 answers 'what happens next?' at a step timescale. Together they supply the trajectory-scoring machinery that E3 will consume in the next step.

tour.title: E3 Trajectory Selector
tour.description: E3 is where deliberation becomes commitment. Given E2-generated candidate trajectories plus the harm/goal/residue costs from downstream substrates, E3TrajectorySelector scores each candidate, applies the ARC-016 dynamic-precision commit gate to decide whether to commit at all, and picks the winning action under a stack of successive constraints — MECH-448 F-eligibility demotion, MECH-449 Go/No-Go, ARC-108 learned per-channel gating, MECH-450 recurrent settling, ARC-110 loop segregation. Reading this file top-to-bottom is a compressed history of every conversion-ceiling fix the project has made.

tour.title: Hippocampus + Residue Memory
tour.description: The hippocampal module generates the candidate trajectories E3 scores — CEM proposals over action-object space O with support-preserving diversity, plus ghost-goal probes, MECH-269 anchor sets with V_s vintaging, and policy chunking/decomposition. The residue field is the complementary long-term memory: an RBF accumulator over world_delta storing four-component valence vectors (wanting / liking / harm-discriminative / surprise, SD-014), plus DA-modulated cluster allocation (SD-024) and safety terrains (SD-052). Together these give the agent both a trajectory imagination store and a lasting map of what mattered where.

tour.title: Cingulate + PFC Control Layer
tour.description: Above the hippocampal/residue substrate sits a bank of control-layer modules that shape how E3 chooses. The salience coordinator (SD-032a) aggregates a dACC bundle plus interoceptive/attention signals into a soft operating-mode distribution and a MECH-261 write-gate registry that gates every downstream substrate. The lateral PFC analog (SD-033a) maintains a persistent rule_state driven by those gates and projects a trainable per-candidate score bias back into E3. This is REE's answer to 'why is the agent doing THIS task right now?'.

tour.title: The Embodied Task Substrate
tour.description: CausalGridWorld is the environment every experiment runs in. It is a large 2D gridworld simulator with hazard/resource/waypoint fields, microhabitat zones, multi-source drift and interoceptive noise, SD-022 directional limb damage, SD-047 multi-source dynamics, SD-049 multi-resource heterogeneity, SD-054 reef refuges, and dozens of other env-only knobs added incrementally as new mechanisms needed testable behavioural signatures. Understanding this file is what tells you what an 'experiment' actually looks like from the agent's sensors.

tour.title: Sleep + Consolidation Loop
tour.description: Sleep is not an afterthought here — it is a first-class phase of the REE loop. SleepLoopManager orchestrates the SD-017 WAKING -> SWS -> PHASE_SWITCH -> REM -> WRITEBACK cycle every K episodes, wiring the MECH-272 routing gate, MECH-275 Bayesian aggregator, MECH-273 self-model writeback, MECH-285 replay sampler, and MECH-476 offline policy window. This is where consolidation, precision recalibration, and offline anchor updating happen; a run with sleep disabled behaves very differently from a run with the SD-017 cluster on.

tour.title: Fleet Coordinator (HTTP + DB + Sync)
tour.description: Now leave the cognitive substrate and enter the second half of the codebase: the fleet coordinator. app.py is the stdlib HTTP server that arbitrates queue claims and ingests result manifests, heartbeats, and shutdown notices from workers. db.py is the SQLite persistence layer holding the queue state machine, claim arbitration, and per-machine telemetry. sync_daemon.py reconciles the DB with the git-authoritative experiment queue and, in Phase 3, is the sole git writer for evidence — carefully guarded against the autostash-driven silent reverts that once plagued the fleet. These three files run on the hub machine 24/7 and are what makes REE a distributed research programme rather than a single-laptop toy.

tour.title: Coordinator Schema + Operator Guide
tour.description: The coordinator's semantics are pinned by two things: the SQL schema that defines what state can exist, and the operator guide that describes how humans drive it in production. schema.sql declares five tables — experiments (the queue), results (manifest bytes with received_at/committed_at timestamps), heartbeats, commands (the coordinator-transport command channel that replaced git command-files), and claim_log (audit trail for legacy git-mutex arbitration). OPERATOR_GUIDE.md documents the three-system architecture (git + coordinator API + sync_daemon writers), the five-phase cutover, and the troubleshooting playbook. Together they close the loop: this is how the cognitive experiments in ree_core/ actually get scheduled, run across the fleet, and land as evidence in REE_assembly/.
tour.languageLesson: SQL: schema.sql is a compact tour of coordination-primitive design — five tables covering queue state, materialised artifacts, telemetry, RPC-style commands, and an audit log, with partial indexes (idx_commands_pending on WHERE acked_at IS NULL) instead of full-column indexes to keep write cost down. Reading the schema before the operator guide is faster than the other way around.
